stem: There are four amendments to the U.S. Constitution about who can vote. Describe one of them.
choices: You must pass a reading test to vote.
Citizens eighteen (18) and older can vote.
Only people who own land can vote.
Noncitizens can vote in federal elections.
oneLineConcept: Voting amendments: race, women, no poll tax, age 18
explanation:
**One voting amendment says citizens eighteen and older can vote.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: You don't have to pay (a poll tax) to vote, Any citizen can vote (women and men can vote), A male citizen of any race (can vote).

**Wrong choices**
- Only people who own land can vote.: The Constitution does not limit voting to landowners.
- You must pass a reading test to vote.: No amendment requires a reading test to vote.
- Noncitizens can vote in federal elections.: Only citizens can vote in federal elections.

stem: Who can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury in the United States?
choices: Anyone living in the United States
Anyone who pays taxes
Lawful permanent residents
U.S. citizens
oneLineConcept: Only citizens vote federally, run for office, serve on juries
explanation:
**Only U.S. citizens can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: Citizens, Citizens of the United States.

**Wrong choices**
- Lawful permanent residents: Green card holders cannot vote in federal elections or serve on a jury.
- Anyone who pays taxes: Paying taxes does not give the right to vote.
- Anyone living in the United States: Only citizens have these rights.

stem: What are three rights of everyone living in the United States?
choices: Right to a government job, right to free college, right to free housing
Right to skip taxes, right to ignore laws, right to avoid jury duty
Freedom of speech, freedom of religion, freedom of assembly
Right to vote, right to run for federal office, right to serve on a jury
oneLineConcept: Rights of everyone: speech, religion, assembly, petition
explanation:
**Freedom of speech, freedom of religion, and freedom of assembly are rights of everyone living in the United States.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: Freedom of expression, Freedom to petition the government, The right to bear arms.

**Wrong choices**
- Right to vote, right to run for federal office, right to serve on a jury: These rights are only for citizens, not everyone living in the U.S.
- Right to a government job, right to free college, right to free housing: These are not rights in the Constitution.
- Right to skip taxes, right to ignore laws, right to avoid jury duty: No one has these rights. Everyone must obey the law.

stem: What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance?
choices: Your home country
The President
Your state governor
The United States
oneLineConcept: Pledge of Allegiance: loyalty to the U.S. and the flag
explanation:
**When we say the Pledge of Allegiance, we show loyalty to the United States.**
Other answer USCIS accepts: The flag.

**Wrong choices**
- The President: The pledge is to the country, not to one person.
- Your home country: New citizens show loyalty to the United States.
- Your state governor: The pledge is not to a governor.

stem: Name two promises that new citizens make in the Oath of Allegiance.
choices: Join a political party, Live in one state forever
Keep loyalty to your home country, Vote in every election
Speak only English at home, Buy a house
Defend the U.S. Constitution, Obey the laws of the United States
oneLineConcept: Oath: give up other loyalty, defend Constitution, obey laws
explanation:
**Two promises in the Oath of Allegiance are to defend the Constitution and obey the laws of the United States.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: Give up loyalty to other countries, Serve in the military (if needed), Serve (help, do important work for) the nation (if needed), Be loyal to the United States.

**Wrong choices**
- Keep loyalty to your home country, Vote in every election: New citizens give up loyalty to other countries. The oath does not require voting in every election.
- Join a political party, Live in one state forever: The oath does not include these promises.
- Speak only English at home, Buy a house: The oath does not include these promises.

stem: How can people become United States citizens?
choices: Naturalize
Buy a house in the United States
Live in the United States for one month
Get a driver’s license
explanation:
**People can become U.S. citizens by naturalizing.** Naturalization is the legal process that immigrants go through to become citizens.
Other answers USCIS accepts: Be born in the United States, under the conditions set by the 14th Amendment; Derive citizenship (under conditions set by Congress).

**Wrong choices**
- Buy a house in the United States: Owning property does not make someone a citizen.
- Get a driver’s license: A driver's license does not give citizenship.
- Live in the United States for one month: Living here a short time does not make someone a citizen.

stem: What are two examples of civic participation in the United States?
choices: Watch TV, Go shopping
Renew a passport, Pay a parking ticket
Avoid jury duty, Skip elections
Vote, Contact elected officials
oneLineConcept: Civic participation: vote, run for office, contact officials
explanation:
**Voting and contacting elected officials are examples of civic participation.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: Run for office, Join a political party, Help with a campaign, Join a civic group, Join a community group, Give an elected official your opinion, Support or oppose an issue or policy, Write to a newspaper.

**Wrong choices**
- Avoid jury duty, Skip elections: These are ways to stay out of civic life, not take part in it.
- Watch TV, Go shopping: These are personal activities, not civic participation.
- Renew a passport, Pay a parking ticket: These are personal tasks, not ways to take part in government.

stem: What is one way Americans can serve their country?
choices: Give up your citizenship
Avoid paying taxes
Ignore court orders
Serve in the military
oneLineConcept: Serve the country: vote, pay taxes, obey law, military
explanation:
**Serving in the military is one way Americans can serve their country.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: Vote, Pay taxes, Obey the law, Run for office, Work for local, state, or federal government.

**Wrong choices**
- Avoid paying taxes: Paying taxes is a way to serve. Avoiding them breaks the law.
- Ignore court orders: Obeying the law serves the country.
- Give up your citizenship: This does not serve the country.

stem: Why is it important to pay federal taxes?
choices: Required by law
To pay for political party campaigns
To buy U.S. citizenship
Only business owners must pay them
oneLineConcept: Federal taxes are required by law and fund the government
explanation:
**It is important to pay federal taxes because it is required by law.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: All people pay to fund the federal government, Required by the (U.S.) Constitution (16th Amendment), Civic duty.

**Wrong choices**
- Only business owners must pay them: All people with taxable income must pay federal taxes.
- To pay for political party campaigns: Taxes fund the federal government, not party campaigns.
- To buy U.S. citizenship: Paying taxes does not buy citizenship.

stem: It is important for all men age 18 through 25 to register for the Selective Service. Name one reason why.
choices: To receive a free college education
Makes the draft fair, if needed
To get a U.S. passport faster
To be able to vote in state elections
oneLineConcept: Selective Service: required by law, makes draft fair
explanation:
**Registering for the Selective Service makes the draft fair, if a draft is ever needed.**
Other answers USCIS accepts: Required by law, Civic duty.

**Wrong choices**
- To be able to vote in state elections: Registering does not give voting rights.
- To receive a free college education: Registering does not give free college.
- To get a U.S. passport faster: Registering does not speed up a passport.
